q: Electroplating is a process where a coating of metal is added to a conductor using electricity via a _____ reaction.
e: Electroplating is a process where a coating of metal is added to a conductor using electricity via a reduction reaction. Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal. Reduction is the word this version is asking about.

Electroplating is also known as electrodeposition. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

q: Electroplating is used to improve the appearance of the metal and to prevent the _____ of metal.
e: Electroplating is used to improve the appearance of the metal and to prevent the corrosion of metal. Corrosion is the oxidation of a metal by air and water. rusting of iron is the common case. Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

q: In electroplating, the _____ is the object to be plated.
e: In electroplating, the cathode is the object to be plated. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs. Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

q: In electroplating, the electrolytic solution must contain ions of the _____ metal for plating.
e: In electroplating, the electrolytic solution must contain ions of the same metal for plating. Electroplating uses electrolysis to coat an object with a thin layer of metal.

q: In silver plating, articles such as spoons or ornaments made of base alloys (e.g., cupronickel) are used as the _____.
e: In silver plating, articles such as spoons or ornaments made of base alloys (e.g., cupronickel) are used as the cathode. An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, made to improve strength or resistance. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: The electrolyte used in silver plating is _____ solution.
e: The electrolyte used in silver plating is potassium argentocyanide solution. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: In silver plating, the anode is made of _____.
e: In silver plating, the anode is made of pure silver. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: In silver plating, the reaction at the anode is $Ag(s) \rightarrow$ _____.
e: In silver plating, the reaction at the anode is Ag(s) to Ag^+(aq) + e^-. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: In chromium plating, a steel object is plated first with nickel or copper, because chromium does not _____ well onto a steel surface.
e: In chromium plating, a steel object is plated first with nickel or copper, because chromium does not stick well onto a steel surface. This is because chromium does not stick well onto a steel surface. Stick is the word this version is asking about.

q: In chromium plating, the object is used as cathode in a plating bath containing acidified _____ solution.
e: In chromium plating, the object is used as cathode in a plating bath containing acidified chromium(III) sulphate solution. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: In chromium plating, the anode is made of _____.
e: In chromium plating, the anode is made of lead. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: In chromium plating, the reaction at the cathode is $Cr^{3+}(aq) + 3e^- \rightarrow$ _____.
e: In chromium plating, the reaction at the cathode is Cr^3+(aq) + 3e^- to Cr(s). The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.
